g1.label: 1. Formal opening
g1.why: “I am writing to …” is the standard formal opening; the alternatives are casual.

g2.correct: I would appreciate it if you could
accept: I would appreciate it if you could
g2.label: 2. Polite request
g2.why: This is the polite formal request; “ASAP” and “You need to” sound demanding.

g3.label: 3. Please find the report ___
g3.why: Documents sent with an email are “attached” — “please find attached” is the fixed phrase.

g4.correct: Should you require any further information
accept: Should you require any further information
g4.label: 4. Offering further information
g4.why: This inverted conditional is the formal register; the others are informal.

g5.label: 5. Thank you for your prompt ___
g5.why: “Prompt response” is the standard formal collocation.

g6.correct: look forward to hearing from you
accept: look forward to hearing from you
g6.label: 6. Formal closing
g6.why: The fixed closing formula — note “to hearing”, not “to hear”.

g7.label: 7. I am writing ___ your order
g7.why: “With regard to” is the formal equivalent of “about”.

g8.label: 8. We sincerely ___
g8.why: “We sincerely apologise for …” is the formal apology; “feel bad about” is conversational.

g1.correct: Thank you for your prompt response.
accept: Thank you for your prompt response.
g1.label: 1. “Thanks for getting back to me so fast.”
g1.why: Same meaning, formal register — thanking someone for replying quickly.

g2.correct: Please accept my apologies for the delayed response.
accept: Please accept my apologies for the delayed response.
g2.label: 2. “Sorry for the late reply.”
g2.why: The formal way to apologise for lateness.

g3.correct: I would be grateful if you could forward the file.
accept: I would be grateful if you could forward the file.
g3.label: 3. “Can you send me the file?”
g3.why: This is a request; the other options describe sending, not asking.

g4.correct: Please do not hesitate to contact me should you require any further assistance.
accept: Please do not hesitate to contact me should you require any further assistance.
g4.label: 4. “Let me know if you need anything else.”
g4.why: The standard formal offer of further help.

g5.correct: I am writing with regard to the issue concerning our order.
accept: I am writing with regard to the issue concerning our order.
g5.label: 5. “I’m writing because of the problem with our order.”
g5.why: States the reason for writing in formal register.

g6.correct: We look forward to your attendance.
accept: We look forward to your attendance.
g6.label: 6. “Hope to see you there!”
g6.why: The formal equivalent of an informal hope to see someone.
